title: Stereotaxic Injection by Nanoject Protocol
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
materials: Preparation and Take Down for Surgical Procedures
Sterilized Surgical Tool Set in Autoclave Tray
Scalpel handle (Fine Science Tools 10003-12 or equivalent)
Iris forceps (Fine Science Tools 11064-07 or equivalent)

Materials (Please note this section is a catch-all for all procedures, not all supplies and equipment are used for every surgical procedure. Refer to SOPs for complete list of required supplies for each specific procedure.)
Nair Hair Removal Cream (Amazon B00R4HWYNI or equivalent)
Black Tempura Paint (Sargent Art 22-7185 or equivalent)
Sugi pointed sterile swabs (Kettenbach 3061 or equivalent)
Sterile Drill Bits, 0.5/0.4 (NeoBurr FG1/4 or equivalent)
Sterile Drill Bits, 1.4/1.1 (NeoBurr FG4 or equivalent)
Sterile Drill Bits 1.0/4.2 (NeoBurr EF4 or equivalent)
Non-Sterile Gloves (Microflex Ultraform Gloves or equivalent)
Kwik Cast (World Precision Instruments Kwik-Cast or equivalent)

steps.title: Prepare Sterile Surgery Area
steps.instruction: Prepare the surgical environment and sterile supplies before animal preparation.

substeps.instruction: Remove hand jewelry, wash hands with soap and water, don exam gloves, and spray with alcohol.
Turn on microscope lights, bead sterilizer, and heating pad (set to 37.0 ± 0.5°C).
Spray surgery area with disinfectant spray cleaner, wait 5 minutes, and wipe with kimwipes.
Wipe down surgical rig, heating pad, nose cone, bite bar, light casings, stereotaxic knobs, and microscope surfaces with alcohol.
Wipe down drill and drill stand with alcohol.
Clean isoflurane induction chamber with disinfectant spray.
Place a sterile drape on the disinfected area, white side up and blue side down.
Drop sterile cotton swabs, kimwipes, and gauze onto the drape without touching them.
Place sterilized surgery tools on the drape, avoiding the instrument tips.
If required, spray a well from the designated jar with 70% Ethanol and place on the drape.
Cover the heating pad on the surgical rig with Press ‘n’ Seal.

steps.title: Prepare ACSF Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare sterile Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid (ACSF) for use during surgery.

substeps.instruction: Fill a 10 or 20 ml syringe with sterile ACSF.
Attach a 25G 5/8” needle to a sterile 0.2 μm syringe filter, then attach the ACSF syringe to the filter.
Expel fluid from the syringe through the filter (do not pull fluid back through the needle).
Place the assembly on the sterile drape.

steps.title: Perform Specific Setup for Headpost/Ephys/C
steps.instruction: Complete additional setup if performing HP Transcranial, HP Ephys, or HP+C procedures.

substeps.instruction: Fill one well with 1 ml Nair.
Fill one well with 1 ml Betadine solution and soak three swabs.
Fill three wells with black cement powder (premixed 4:1 cement to paint) if required.
For HP+C: Use sterile forceps to place pieces of sterile Gelfoam in one well.
Place a coverslip in a well and cover with 70% Ethanol to soak using forceps.
Fill the Gelfoam well with ACSF to soak.
Fill one or two wells with ACSF.
Disinfect drill with 70% Ethanol and attach the drill bit.

steps.title: Prepare Nanoject Pipette and Virus
steps.instruction: Prepare the Nanoject-specific pipette and load it with the virus.

substeps.instruction: Obtain a Nanoject-specific pipette (pulled and broken at the proper distance).
Remove virus aliquot from -80ºC freezer, thaw at room temperature, spin down in mini centrifuge, and store on wet ice.
Fill one well of a 24-well plate with Betadine and a second with Nair; place on sterile drape.
Backfill the pipette using a 30g, 2” Hamilton syringe filled with mineral oil by inserting the syringe tip to the shoulder and slowly depressing the plunger.
Set the Nanoject wire plunger to the 'home position' (tip flush with or slightly recessed from the end of the collet).
Insert the blunt end of the pipette through the collet and large O-ring, pushing it onto the wire plunger until it seats in the white spacer, then tighten the collet.
Press and hold the 'EMPTY' button to expel 4-5 drops of oil and remove air bubbles (do not extend plunger to full length).
Spin down virus for 10-15 seconds, draw up ~2 µl using a P20 micropipette with microfil tip, and aspirate onto Parafilm.
Lower the Nanoject pipette tip into the virus sample and press/hold the 'FILL' button to draw up the desired amount.
Set volume switches 1-5 to D-D-U-D-D for a standard injection of 50.6 nl per press at 23 nl/sec (unless otherwise specified).

steps.title: Prepare Anesthesia System
steps.instruction: Configure the gas delivery system for animal induction and maintenance.

substeps.instruction: Set vacuum gauge to 10-15 PSI and verify all vacuum lines.
Connect induction chamber to Isoflurane and Oxygen.
Turn on oxygen concentrator and set Oxygen regulator to 0.8-1.0 L/min.
Open vacuum and Isoflurane valves and direct flow to the induction chamber.

steps.title: Induce Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse and transfer it to the surgical rig.

substeps.instruction: Record preoperative weight, cage number, sex, and birthdate.
Place mouse in induction chamber and set Isoflurane regulator to 5.0 (5%), noting the start time.
Once unconscious (approx. one breath every 3 seconds), turn off Isoflurane but keep oxygen and vacuum lines open while removing the mouse.
Position mouse on the surgical rig using ear bars or specified clamps.
Secure the nose cone over the snout, ensure the body is on the heating pad, and redirect gas flow to the rig.
Set Isoflurane to ~1.5-2% and turn off the induction chamber vacuum line.
Monitor breathing and toe-pinch response, adjusting Isoflurane levels as necessary.

steps.title: Prepare Surgical Site
steps.instruction: Clear and disinfect the head area for the incision.

substeps.instruction: Use a cotton swab with Puralube to push whiskers away from the field and cover eyes with Puralube.
Secure ear bars into ear canals or temples, ensuring the head is straight, symmetrical, and immobile.
Use non-sterile scissors to shorten hair from the top of the head and left side of the face (behind ears and between eyes). Wipe scissors with alcohol after use.
Apply Nair with a non-sterile cotton swab; remove within 25 seconds.
Remove all Nair using clean, non-sterile cotton swabs or alcohol wipes (one swipe per swab).
Wipe head surface with ACSF or alcohol wipes and clean with kimwipes.
Disinfect head with 3 rounds of alternating Betadine-soaked sterile swabs and alcohol wipes; do not wipe off the final Betadine application.
Discard the hair-catch gauze from under the mouse into a biohazard bin.
Cover the mouse's body up to the surgical site with saran wrap.

steps.title: Post-Operative Take-down
steps.instruction: Clean the surgical area and sterilize tools after the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Change gloves after removing the animal from the rig and completing immediate post-op care.
Disinfect the surgery area as per the initial setup steps.
Dispose of syringes, blades, drill bits, and needles in biohazard sharps containers.

Spray tools with pH neutral surgical tool cleaner, wipe clean of blood/skin/cement, wrap in autoclave packs with initials and date, and take to autoclave (or use hot bead sterilizer for same-day use).
Disinfect ear bars with 70% Ethanol.
Release air from drill lines (0 psi) and turn off wall valves.
Switch vacuum and oxygen stopcocks to the off position.

description: General principles for “tips only” aseptic surgery
